汤隆者，延安府人氏也。其父原是延安府的一个老军，专管打造军器，乃是个出色的铁匠。.en:
Tang Long was a native of Yan'an Prefecture. His father was an old soldier there, responsible for making military equipment and an excellent blacksmith. From childhood Tang Long learned the trade at his father's side. He could forge swords, spears, halberds, axes, and every other kind of weapon, becoming an armorer of the first rank. His face was dark and sallow, and his body was covered with scabs, ringworm, and sores, leaving spots and patches all over him. Seeing this, people in the martial world gave him the nickname “Spotted Leopard”: his mottled skin resembled the coin-shaped markings of a leopard. He also wielded an iron melon-headed hammer with considerable strength, so the name suggested not only his appearance but something of his ferocity. After his father died, Tang Long drifted through the world, earning a wandering living by forging metal for others.

He joined Liangshan through a chance meeting. Li Kui encountered him on a journey away from the mountain, and the two came to know each other by first exchanging blows. After testing him, Li Kui saw that he had some ability and was also a blacksmith, so he invited him to Liangshan. Tang Long had long heard the heroes' reputation and gladly followed. He joined the brotherhood as the commander overseeing the manufacture of weapons and all manner of blades and armor. His smithcraft contributed greatly to the sound armor and fine equipment that Liangshan's army later possessed.

His greatest achievement was devising the scheme to lure Xu Ning to the mountain and proposing hooked lances to defeat the linked cavalry. Huyan Zhuo had chained three thousand horses together with iron rings, armoring both riders and mounts. Their charge fell like a collapsing wall, inflicting heavy losses on Liangshan in repeated encounters and leaving Song Jiang deeply troubled. Tang Long stepped forward with a solution: a weapon called the hooked lance, whose hooked head could catch horses' legs. Once the linked mounts were pulled down, their formation would collapse. Asked who could make and teach these weapons, he replied that he knew how to forge them. Only one man, however, fully mastered their use: Xu Ning the Golden Lancer, instructor of the Eastern Capital's Golden Lance corps. Xu Ning was Tang Long's cousin, described as a cousin through his aunt, and his family's inherited hooked-lance art was unrivaled. Tang Long proposed exploiting Xu Ning's most precious heirloom, a suit of gold-ringed armor with overlapping goose-feather scales, called Sai Tangni. Xu Ning valued it as his life. Shi Qian, the Flea on a Drum, would enter the capital and steal it, drawing Xu Ning out in pursuit. Tang Long would then intercept him and lead him step by step toward Liangshan. The plan was carried out: Shi Qian stole the armor, and Tang Long disguised himself as a traveling merchant, drew Xu Ning onward, and finally drugged him unconscious to bring him up the mountain. Once there, Xu Ning joined the brotherhood and taught the troops the hooked-lance technique. They shattered Huyan Zhuo's linked cavalry and reversed the course of the battle. The entire exploit, from tricking Xu Ning to destroying the linked horses, was planned and brought about by Tang Long. It was the foremost achievement of his life and showed that this blacksmith possessed cunning as well as skill at the forge.

When Liangshan's great assembly assigned the Heavenly and Earthly Star seats, Tang Long answered to the Earthly Solitary Star and ranked eighty-eighth among the Earthly Stars. He supervised the manufacture of weapons and iron armor, an indispensable master craftsman in the army. With his iron melon-headed hammer he could fight in battle, but his true gift lay in his deft smith's hands rather than in leading charges.

After the amnesty, Tang Long served with Song Jiang against Liao, Tian Hu, and Wang Qing. The army relied on him to replace damaged weapons and repair armor on campaign. In the terrible southern expedition against Fang La, more than half Liangshan's commanders were killed or wounded. Tang Long accompanied the army and was wounded by a spear in the fighting around Shezhou. Treatment failed, and he died of his injuries in Jiangnan, never returning home. From a blacksmith of Yan'an to the architect of Xu Ning's recruitment and the defeat of the linked cavalry, the Spotted Leopard ultimately died for the country in Fang La's campaign. Though craftsmanship was his chief talent, his strategy, loyalty, and courage secured him a memorable place among the 108 heroes.
汤隆者，延安府人氏也。其父原是延安府的一个老军，专管打造军器，乃是个出色的铁匠。.ja:
湯隆は延安府の出身である。父は延安府の老兵で、軍器の製造を担当する優れた鍛冶師だった。湯隆は幼い頃から父について技を学び、刀槍剣戟、戈矛斧鉞と、作れぬ武器のない一流の軍器職人となった。顔は黒ずんだ黄色で、全身に疥癬や皮膚病の瘡があり、点々と斑が広がっていた。その姿を見た江湖の人々は「金銭豹子」と呼んだ。銭のような豹の斑紋に似た、全身の斑点を表す名である。また鉄の瓜形の槌を使い、戦場でも相応の力を示したため、この異名には容貌だけでなく勇猛さも含まれていた。父が死ぬと江湖を流浪し、各地で人に頼まれて鉄を鍛えながら、不定の暮らしを送った。

梁山泊入りのきっかけは偶然の出会いだった。下山していた李逵と道中で出会い、まず争って腕を試した後に互いを知った。李逵は湯隆に腕があり、しかも鍛冶師だと分かると、共に梁山へ上ろうと誘った。梁山の好漢の名声をかねて聞いていた湯隆は喜んで従い、軍器の製造と刀槍甲冑一切の監督を担う総管頭領となった。後に梁山の兵甲が整い、軍器が優れたものとなったのは、彼の鍛冶の技によるところが大きい。

梁山での最大の功績は、徐寧を計略で山へ招き、鉤鎌槍で連環馬を破る策を献じたことである。当時、呼延灼は三千頭の馬を鉄環でつなぎ、人馬ともに甲冑で固めた連環馬陣を敷いた。その突進は壁が崩れ落ちるようで、梁山は幾度戦っても大きな損害を受け、宋江は深く悩んでいた。湯隆は進み出て、これを破るには穂先に鉤のある鉤鎌槍で馬の脚を引っ掛ければよく、つながれた馬を倒せば陣は保てないと述べた。製法と使い方を誰から学ぶのかと問われると、製造は自分にできるが、その武芸に精通するのは天下でただ一人、東京の金槍班教師「金槍手」徐寧だけだと答えた。徐寧は湯隆の姑舅の兄、すなわち従兄に当たり、家伝の鉤鎌槍法は天下に並ぶものがなかった。そこで湯隆は一計を献じた。徐寧には「賽唐猊」と呼ばれる、雁の羽状の鱗を重ねた雁翎圏金甲という家宝があり、命ほど大切にしている。まず鼓上蚤時遷を東京に忍び込ませて宝甲を盗み、徐寧を追跡のため都の外へ誘い出す。その途中で湯隆が迎え、一歩ずつ梁山へ導こうというのである。皆が策に従うと、時遷は見事に宝甲を盗み、湯隆は通りがかりの商人を装って徐寧を誘導し、さらに眠り薬で昏倒させて山へ連れてきた。徐寧は入山すると仲間になることを決め、兵士たちに鉤鎌槍法を教えた。梁山は呼延灼の連環馬を大いに破り、戦局を逆転させた。「湯隆が徐寧を計って招く」「鉤鎌槍が連環馬を大破する」という一連の働きは、すべて湯隆が考え、実現したものだった。生涯第一の奇功であり、鍛冶師出身の好漢が鉄を打つだけでなく、知略も備えていたことを示している。

梁山の大聚義で天罡地煞の席次が定まると、湯隆は地孤星に応じ、地煞の第八十八位に座した。さまざまな軍器と鉄甲の製造を専ら監督する、軍に不可欠な工匠頭領である。鉄の瓜槌を使って戦場で戦うこともできたが、真価は突撃の働きよりも、鉄を鍛える巧みな両手にあった。

招安の後は宋公明に従って遼国、田虎、王慶を征し、軍中で力を尽くした。軍器が壊れ、甲冑の修理が必要になれば、多くは彼が従軍して製造、修繕した。方臘への南征は梁山頭領の半数以上が死傷する激戦となった。湯隆も軍と共に進み、歙州一帯の戦いで槍傷を負った。治療の甲斐なく重傷のため江南で死に、故郷へ生きて帰ることはなかった。延安府の鍛冶師に始まり、連環馬を破る策と徐寧の招致で奇功を立て、最後は大義に従って方臘征討に殉じた「金銭豹子」湯隆。その得意は工匠の技であったが、知略と忠勇もまた、百八将の中に語り継ぐべき事績を残すに十分だった。

陶宗旺，绰号「九尾龟」，光州人氏，应地理星，于梁山泊一百单八将中坐第七十五把交椅.en:
Tao Zongwang, nicknamed “Nine-Tailed Turtle,” was a native of Guangzhou. Answering to the Earthly Geography Star, he held the seventy-fifth seat among Liangshan Marsh's 108 heroes and served as an infantry commander. Born a farmer, he was sturdy and immensely strong. His usual weapon was an iron shovel, though he could also wield spear and saber, making him one of the few Liangshan heroes to fight with a farm tool and rely chiefly on strength. His nickname praised his deep endurance and ability to bear heavy burdens. An expert at digging earth, building defenses, cutting ditches, and channeling water, he resembled the mythical nine-tailed turtle that carries an immense weight and advances steadily over great distances.

Though raised on the land, Tao Zongwang would not spend his whole life in the fields. Relying on his strength and martial skill, he entered the world of wandering heroes and became an outlaw at Huangmen Mountain. The bandit stronghold had four chiefs: Ou Peng, the Golden Wings Brushing the Clouds, came first; Jiang Jing the Divine Calculator second; Ma Lin the Iron Flute Immortal third; and Tao Zongwang the Nine-Tailed Turtle fourth. They formed a mountain brotherhood, raiding and robbing, and dominated the region. As the fourth leader, Tao Zongwang managed land clearance, fort construction, military farming, and waterworks. With his iron shovel he dug trenches and built obstacles, performing much arduous labor. No one in the stronghold bore hard work and heavy loads more willingly.

Their allegiance to Liangshan began with Song Jiang's ordeal in Jiangzhou. After he wrote a rebellious poem at Xunyang Tower, Huang Wenbing denounced him, and he was imprisoned and nearly executed. Chao Gai led Liangshan's heroes to raid the execution ground and rescue Song Jiang and Dai Zong. They fought their way to White Dragon Temple to regroup, then burned through Wuweijun and captured Huang Wenbing alive to avenge the wrong. When it was over, Song Jiang led the old and new heroes back toward Liangshan, passing beneath Huangmen Mountain. The four chiefs had long heard the name of Song Jiang, the Timely Rain, and already wished to join him. They brought their band down, stopped the travelers, and bowed, declaring themselves ready to leave their small stronghold and join Liangshan's great cause. Delighted, Song Jiang accepted them. Tao Zongwang thus went with his three Huangmen brothers to Liangshan. This recruitment on the return from the Jiangzhou rescue, around the episode in which Song Jiang meets the Mystic Lady of the Nine Heavens and receives three heavenly books at Huandao Village, marks Tao Zongwang's appearance in the original novel.

His farming and construction skills proved useful at Liangshan. He contributed to the walls of the water stronghold and the excavation of defensive ditches. In his hands the iron shovel could kill an enemy or clear a hillside and work the soil: he was a rare practical talent in the army. At the great ranking he took the seventy-fifth seat as the Earthly Geography Star, an apt name for a man skilled in reading terrain and building fortifications. He served with Ou Peng, Ma Lin, and others in the infantry, charging with the main force. Though not a foremost champion famed for cutting down generals, he was indispensable when attacking strongpoints, defending difficult ground, and building camps and ramparts.

After the court granted amnesty, Tao Zongwang marched with Song Jiang against Liao and, under imperial orders, against Tian Hu in Hebei and Wang Qing in Huaixi. Over years of fighting north and south, his strength carried him safely through many dangerous battles. Yet he could not escape the devastating losses of the Fang La campaign in Jiangnan. During the attack on Runzhou, he fought Fang La's troops and was killed in the confused clash, dying in imperial service and shedding his blood in Jiangnan. The shovel that had cleared hills, channeled water, and raised forts lay buried forever on the southern battlefield. When the court recorded the generals killed in defeating Fang La, Tao Zongwang received posthumous honors and a place among the loyal. The Nine-Tailed Turtle had risen from the fields with his ambitions set on the wider world, beginning at Huangmen Mountain and ending in Song Jiang's service. He did not boast of slain generals; his standing came from bearing burdens, accepting toil, and working diligently. His loyal and courageous death upheld the Liangshan heroes' reputation for valuing duty above life.
陶宗旺，绰号「九尾龟」，光州人氏，应地理星，于梁山泊一百单八将中坐第七十五把交椅.ja:
陶宗旺は「九尾亀」の異名を持つ光州出身の好漢で、地理星に応じ、梁山泊百八将の第七十五位に座す歩軍頭領である。もとは田畑を耕す農民で、体は頑丈、腕力は人に優れ、鉄の鍬を常用し、槍や刀も使えた。農具を武器とし、力を得意とする梁山でも珍しい人物だった。「九尾亀」と呼ばれたのは、重々しい持久力があり、重荷にも耐え、土を掘り、塁を築き、溝を開き、水を引くのに長じていたためである。千鈞の重さを背負っても着実に遠くへ進む九尾の神亀に似ていることから、この名を得た。

農家に生まれた陶宗旺は、田畑だけで一生を終えることを望まず、力と武芸を頼みに江湖へ出て、黄門山で山賊となった。そこには四人の頭領がいた。首領は摩雲金翅欧鵬、第二は神算子蔣敬、第三は鉄笛仙馬麟、第四が九尾亀陶宗旺である。四人は山林に義を結び、家々を襲って略奪し、一帯に勢力を張った。第四の頭領である陶宗旺は、山を開き、寨を築き、屯田し、水を引く仕事を担った。一本の鉄鍬で濠や障害を設けて多くの苦労を重ね、山寨で最もよく骨折りと重荷を引き受ける男だった。

黄門山の一党が梁山へ帰順したのは、宋江の江州での災難に始まる。宋江は潯陽楼に反詩を書き、黄文炳に告発されて江州の牢へ入れられ、処刑されかけた。晁蓋は梁山の好漢を率いて刑場を襲い、宋江と戴宗を救い、白竜廟へ戦い抜いて集結した。さらに無為軍を火で一掃し、黄文炳を生け捕りにして恨みを晴らした。事が済み、宋江が新旧の好漢を連れて梁山へ帰る途中、黄門山の麓を通った。欧鵬、蔣敬、馬麟、陶宗旺は「及時雨」宋公明の名声を久しく聞き、もとより帰順したいと思っていたため、配下を率いて下山し、道を遮ってひれ伏した。黄門山の小寨を捨て、梁山泊の大義に加わりたいと願うと、宋江は大いに喜んで受け入れた。陶宗旺はこうして黄門山の三兄弟と共に梁山へ上った。「還道村で三巻の天書を授かり、宋公明が九天玄女に会う」という挿話の前後、江州の刑場襲撃から帰山する途上で黄門山の一党が加わるくだりが、原作での彼の登場場面である。

梁山では農事と築造の技が大いに役立った。水寨の城壁造りや濠などの工事で力を振るい、その手の鉄鍬は戦場で敵を倒すことも、山を開き土を整えることもできた。軍中では得難い実務の才である。大聚義で席次を定めると第七十五位、地理星となった。「地理」の二字は、地形を見極め工事を営む彼の本領にふさわしい。欧鵬や馬麟らと歩軍を司り、大軍と共に突撃した。敵将を斬る第一級の猛将ではなくとも、堅陣の攻略、険地の防衛、陣営や堡塁の築造に欠かせない一員だった。

梁山が朝廷の招安を受けると、陶宗旺は宋江の大軍と遼国を北征し、さらに勅命を受けて河北の田虎、淮西の王慶を討った。数年にわたる南北の転戦では、優れた力で幾度も危険な戦いをくぐり抜けた。しかし好漢の死傷が甚だしかった江南の方臘征討では、災いを免れなかった。潤州の攻略中、方臘軍と戦い、乱戦の中で命を落として王事に殉じ、血を江南に流した。山を開き、水を引き、寨や塁を築いた鉄鍬は、南征の戦場に永久に埋もれたのである。朝廷が方臘平定の戦没諸将を記録すると、陶宗旺にも追封が与えられ、忠義の名簿に列した。田畑に生まれ江湖を志し、黄門山から身を起こして宋江に従い終えた九尾亀は、敵将を斬った手柄を誇らず、重荷と労苦を担い、地道に働いて身を立てた。最後も忠勇を尽くし、義を重んじ命を惜しまぬ梁山好漢の名に背かなかった。

童猛，浔阳江人氏，乃出洞蛟童威之亲弟，水浒一百单八将中与其兄并肩而立的一对水上豪.en:
Tong Meng came from the Xunyang River and was the younger brother of Tong Wei, the Dragon Emerging from Its Cave. Among Water Margin's 108 heroes, they stood together as a pair of champions of the water. Their family had lived beside the great river for generations, drawing their sustenance from it and relying on swimming skills learned while making a living among winds and waves from childhood. Poverty drove them both into illegal salt trading. They poled and rowed their boats through the misty Xunyang waters, smuggling cargo past the law. Such trade put a man's life at risk and demanded extraordinary aquatic skill and reckless courage. Tong Meng was no less capable in the water than his elder brother. He could churn through raging waves, overturn boats, and retrieve objects underwater. For this he was called the “River-Churning Shen.” The shen was a legendary water creature said to breathe out mirage palaces and stir up water and mist. The name suited his uncanny movements and mastery of the river, while complementing his brother's dragon nickname: together they seemed a pair of water spirits haunting the Xunyang.

Like his brother, Tong Meng became connected to Liangshan through the rescue of Song Jiang at Jieyang Ridge. While being escorted to exile in Jiangzhou, Song Jiang passed through Jieyang Ridge and Jieyang Town, first falling into Li Li's murderous inn and then provoking the anger of the Mu Hong brothers. Forced to flee along the river, he nearly lost his life. Li Jun, the River-Mixing Dragon, came by boat with Tong Wei and Tong Meng, rescued Song Jiang amid the wind and waves of the Xunyang, and mediated the dispute. This is the crucial incident in the chapter titled “At Liangshan Marsh Wu Yong Recommends Dai Zong; At Jieyang Ridge Song Jiang Meets Li Jun.” The debt of gratitude bound the Tong brothers firmly to Liangshan's fate. When Li Jun later joined the mountain stronghold, they abandoned salt smuggling and followed him. The two water spirits thus entered the vast, mist-covered eight hundred li of Liangshan Marsh.

His knowledge of water warfare made Tong Meng one of the naval commanders. With water guarding Liangshan on three sides, the stronghold depended on its skilled swimmers; cutting crossings, seizing provisions, fire attacks, and ambushes all made the fleet vital. At the great ranking, Tong Meng took the sixty-ninth seat as the Earthly Retreating Star. With Ruan Xiao'er, the Short-Lived Second Son, he guarded the northwestern water camp, patrolled channels and narrows, and trained boat crews. Tong Wei guarded the northeastern camp. The brothers held separate sectors that supported each other across the broad waters, securing the approaches to the marsh. Though the novel gives Tong Meng relatively little space, he invariably appears beside his brother in naval battles, waving banners, driving oars, and charging the enemy. He was a dependable fighting officer of Liangshan's fleet.

After the amnesty, Tong Meng campaigned in all directions: north against Great Liao, then against Tian Hu and Wang Qing, and finally south against Fang La. Jiangnan's dense network of waterways gave the navy ample scope, and the brothers repeatedly used their river mastery to fight through spears, arrows, flames, and dangerous waves. More than half the Liangshan heroes were lost in this campaign, staining Jiangnan with blood, but Tong Meng's swimming skills carried him through repeated dangers. He became one of the rare survivors of the troubled age's warfare. Once Fang La had been defeated, Li Jun perceived the deadly danger behind official fame and refused to enter the court of wolves and tigers. Pretending to be ill, he remained by the river and secretly arranged for Tong Wei and Tong Meng to wait for him. The three reunited, abandoned the offices and wealth within reach, and sailed from Taicang Harbor across the ocean to Siam. Li Jun later established a realm overseas and became its ruler. Tong Meng and his brother assisted him together and met peaceful ends in a foreign land. The river-churning creature had returned at last to the sea. Avoiding the deaths in battle and the many other sorrowful endings that scattered Liangshan's heroes, Tong Meng and his brother lived beyond the empire, an uncommon instance of a life well begun and well ended among Water Margin's champions.
童猛，浔阳江人氏，乃出洞蛟童威之亲弟，水浒一百单八将中与其兄并肩而立的一对水上豪.ja:
童猛は潯陽江の出身で、出洞蛟童威の実弟である。水滸百八将の中で、兄と肩を並べる一組の水上の豪傑だった。童家の兄弟は代々大河のほとりに住み、川に養われ、水練を頼りに、幼い頃から風波の中で暮らしを立てていた。家計が苦しく、二人とも塩の密売を営み、舟を操って潯陽江の煙波に出没した。塩の密売は国法に触れ、首を懸ける商売であり、人並み以上の水練と命知らずの胆力がなければ務まらない。童猛の水中の技は兄にも劣らず、荒波をかき乱し、舟を覆し、水中から物を取ることができたため、江湖で「翻江蜃」と呼ばれた。蜃は息で楼閣の幻を作り、水を乱して霧を起こすという伝説の水の異物である。川を覆すような技と神出鬼没の泳ぎに似合う異名で、兄の「出洞蛟」とも対を成し、まるで潯陽江に棲む蛟と蜃の二つの精怪のようだった。

梁山との縁は兄と同じく、掲陽嶺で宋江を救った義挙に結ばれている。江州へ刺配される途中の宋江は、掲陽嶺と掲陽鎮で、まず李立の悪徳宿に陥り、次いで穆弘兄弟の怒りに触れ、川沿いを逃げて命を失いかけた。混江竜李俊が童威、童猛と舟を漕いで駆けつけ、潯陽江の風波の中で宋江を救い、仲立ちをして争いを収めたのである。これは「梁山泊で呉用が戴宗を推挙し、掲陽嶺で宋江が李俊に逢う」の回の要所に当たる。この恩義が童家の兄弟と梁山泊の命脈を強く結んだ。後に李俊が入山すると、童威と童猛も塩の密売を捨てて従い、二つの水中の精怪は八百里の梁山泊の広い煙波へ泳ぎ入った。

仲間に加わると、水戦を熟知する童猛は水軍頭領に列した。梁山は三方を水に守られ、山寨の基盤は泳ぎ巧者たちにかかっていた。渡しの遮断、兵糧の奪取、火攻め、伏兵など、水軍の役割は何より重要だった。大聚義で童猛は第六十九位、地退星となり、短命二郎阮小二とともに北西の水寨を守り、川と要路を巡察し、舟師を訓練した。兄の童威は北東の水寨を守った。兄弟は別々の一方を占めて遠く呼応し、広大な碧波の上で互いに支え合い、水泊の入口を押さえた。原作で童猛に割かれる筆は多くないが、水戦のたびに兄と連れ立って旗を振り、櫂を動かし、敵陣へ突入する、水軍の確かな働き手だった。

招安後は大軍に従って各地を転戦し、大遼を北征した後、田虎、王慶を掃討し、最後に方臘を南征した。江南は水路が縦横に走り、水軍が技を振るう場であった。童家の兄弟は幾度も川をかき乱すほどの腕を頼みに、槍と矢、烈火と荒波の中を往来して敵と戦った。この戦役で梁山の好漢は半数以上を失い、血が江南を染めたが、童猛は優れた水練で何度も危険をくぐり抜け、乱世の戦から生き残った数少ない者となった。方臘が平定されると、李俊は功名の背後に潜む殺機を見抜き、虎狼のような朝廷へ入ることを望まなかった。病を装って川辺に残り、童威と童猛には密かに待つよう約束した。三人は合流すると、手に入るはずの官爵と栄華を捨て、太倉港から帆を上げ、海を渡って暹羅国へ向かった。後に李俊は海外で国を興して王となり、童猛と兄は力を合わせて補佐し、異国で安らかな最期を迎えた。江を翻す蜃はついに大海へ帰ったのである。戦死や坐化、離散など梁山の人々の悲しい結末を避け、兄とともに王化の外に生きた童猛は、水滸の群雄の中でも善く始め善く終えた、まれな存在だった。

童威，浔阳江畔人氏，是江州一带有名的水上豪客，与其弟童猛并称「童家二雄」。兄弟二.en:
Tong Wei, born beside the Xunyang River, was a renowned waterborne adventurer in the Jiangzhou region. He and his younger brother Tong Meng were called the Two Heroes of the Tong Family. Their family had lived on the great river's banks for generations, and both learned from childhood to handle wind and waves and master the water. Forced by poverty, they traded in contraband salt. Salt was a government monopoly: private trading could mean death or exile to military service, and only men of courage and strength dared attempt it. In this perilous livelihood, Tong Wei developed formidable skills, moving through waves and storms as easily as walking on level ground. He earned the nickname “Dragon Emerging from Its Cave,” likening him to a dragon that lurks in the depths and raises great waves when it stirs. Rough in appearance but frank in character, he valued loyalty above life. He associated with such river heroes as Li Jun the River-Mixing Dragon and Zhang Heng the Boatman, and was a figure on the Xunyang who troubled the authorities and commanded merchants' wary respect.

His connection to Liangshan began with a rescue at Jieyang Ridge. Song Jiang, traveling into exile at Jiangzhou, entered Li Li's murderous inn and nearly became filling for human-meat buns. Li Jun arrived in time, recognized him, and saved him. Later, in Jieyang Town, Song Jiang offended Mu Hong the Unrestrained and his brother Mu Chun the Lesser Unrestrained. Driven into a desperate flight along the river, he again nearly died. At the crisis, Li Jun arrived by boat with Tong Wei and Tong Meng, rescued him from the Xunyang's terrifying waves, and settled the quarrel. This episode, “At Jieyang Ridge Song Jiang Meets Li Jun,” bound the Tong brothers' destiny firmly to Liangshan. When Li Jun later joined the mountain, both followed him to the marsh, abandoning salt smuggling to enter the loyal brotherhood.

Tong Wei's skill in water warfare earned him a place among the naval commanders. Surrounded by water on three sides amid eight hundred li of misty waves, Liangshan depended on its fleet for survival. Seizing provisions, cutting crossings, fire attacks, and ambushes all relied on the aquatic heroes, of whom Tong Wei was a capable member. At the great ranking he took the sixty-eighth seat as the Earthly Advancing Star. Together with Ruan Xiaowu, the Living King of Hell, he guarded the northeastern water camp, trained the navy day and night, and patrolled the channels and narrows. He formed an indispensable barrier at the marsh's entrance. Tong Meng guarded the northwestern camp, the brothers holding separate corners and supporting each other across the immense expanse of green water.

After the amnesty, Tong Wei followed the army against Liao, Tian Hu, Wang Qing, and finally Fang La. Wherever there was fighting on water, the Tong brothers could be seen waving banners and driving their oars. The Fang La campaign cost more than half the Liangshan heroes, spreading their blood across fertile Jiangnan. Yet Tong Wei's dragonlike mastery of the water brought him alive through repeated deadly dangers, making him one of the rare survivors. After Fang La's defeat, as the court prepared to distribute offices and titles, Li Jun saw the dangers behind fame and the treachery of official life. He pretended to suffer a stroke and stayed by the river to recover, secretly arranging for Tong Wei and Tong Meng to wait for him. The three reunited, abandoned wealth and honors, and sailed from Taicang Harbor across the sea to Siam. Li Jun later made himself ruler overseas, and Tong Wei served at his side, living out his days peacefully abroad in a tale of freedom beyond the empire. Of Liangshan's 108, many died in imperial service; only a few, such as Li Jun and the Tong brothers, withdrew after success and escaped beyond the ocean to preserve their lives. The dragon that emerged from its cave returned at last to the sea: Tong Wei had found a fitting end.
童威，浔阳江畔人氏，是江州一带有名的水上豪客，与其弟童猛并称「童家二雄」。兄弟二.ja:
童威は潯陽江のほとりの出身で、江州一帯に名高い水上の豪客であり、弟の童猛と「童家の二雄」と称された。兄弟は代々大河の岸に住み、幼い頃から風波に慣れて水練に通じていた。暮らしに迫られ、営んでいたのは塩の密売である。塩は官の専売品であり、密売は重ければ死罪、軽くても軍への流刑となるため、胆力と腕力がなければ手を出せなかった。童威はこの命懸けの商売で技を鍛え、水や波の中、風濤に出入りすること平地を行くがごとくだったので、「出洞蛟」の異名を得た。蛟は深淵に潜み、現れれば波を起こすもの。この名は、川底に潜み、一たび動けば幾重もの波を巻き起こす彼の本領をよく表している。姿は荒々しく、性格は率直で、義を重んじ生死を軽んじた。混江竜李俊や船火児張横ら水上の好漢と交わり、潯陽江では役人を悩ませ、商人に畏れられる存在だった。

梁山との縁は、掲陽嶺での人命救助に始まる。江州へ刺配される宋江は掲陽嶺で李立の悪徳宿に入り、あやうく人肉饅頭の具にされるところを、駆けつけた李俊に見つけられて救われた。その後、掲陽鎮で没遮攔穆弘と小遮攔穆春の兄弟の怒りに触れ、川沿いを追われて行き場を失い、またも命を落としかけた。危急の時、李俊が童威、童猛と舟で駆けつけ、潯陽江の激しい波の中から宋江を救い、仲立ちして争いを和解へ導いた。「掲陽嶺で宋江が李俊に逢う」というこの因縁が、童家の兄弟と梁山の運命を固く結んだ。後に李俊が入山すると、二人も水泊へ従い、塩の密売を捨てて忠義の仲間に加わった。

童威は入山後、水戦に優れることから水軍頭領に編入された。三方を水に囲まれ、八百里の煙波を持つ梁山泊では、水軍が山寨の根本であった。兵糧を奪い、渡しを断ち、火攻めや伏兵を仕掛けるにも、泳ぎ巧者の好漢たちが頼りで、童威はその有力な一人だった。大聚義では第六十八位、地進星となり、活閻羅阮小五とともに北東の水寨を守った。日夜水軍を訓練し、川と要路を巡察する、水泊の入口に不可欠な守りである。弟の童猛は北西の水寨を守り、兄弟はそれぞれ一隅に拠って遠く呼応し、万頃の碧波の上で互いを支える態勢を成した。

招安後は大軍に従って遼国、田虎、王慶を征し、最後に方臘を南征した。水戦のある所には必ず、旗を振り櫂を動かす童家の兄弟の姿があった。方臘征討では梁山の好漢が半数以上を失い、肥沃な江南に英雄の血が広く流れたが、童威は蛟竜のような水練を頼みに幾度も死地をくぐり、乱軍の中で生き残った数少ない者となった。方臘が平定され、朝廷が功に応じて官爵を授けようとした時、李俊は功名の裏に潜む凶事と官界の険悪さを見抜いた。中風を患ったと偽って川辺に残り、童威と童猛に密かに待ち合わせを頼んだ。三人は合流して栄華富貴を捨て、太倉港から舟で海へ出て、遠く暹羅国へ渡った。後に李俊は海外で王となり、童威はその側で補佐して異国で安らかに生涯を終え、王化の外で自由に暮らす伝説を残した。梁山百八人のうち王事に死んだ者は多く、功成って退き、海天の彼方へ逃れて命を全うできたのは、李俊と童家兄弟らわずかな者だけであった。洞を出た蛟はついに大海へ帰り、童威はふさわしい最期を得たのである。

王定六者，建康人氏，水浒一百单八将中一员脚力极健、来去如飞的好汉。其人在江边卖酒.en:
Wang Dingliu, a native of Jiankang, was one of Water Margin's 108 heroes, a man whose extraordinarily strong legs carried him as if in flight. He sold wine beside the river, practiced spear and staff, and was skilled with fists and feet. Exceptionally impatient, he did everything in a rush, his feet seeming to raise wind whenever he walked. His remarkable speed earned him the nickname “Living Lightning.” Shan means a flash of light, and huoshan is the Jiangnan expression for lightning; the final syllable po serves as an added expression emphasizing a lightning flash's speed. The name thus described his fleet feet and electric pace. Though it sounded less imposing than many heroes' titles, it vividly captured his gift for running.

His family and livelihood were thoroughly respectable. He and his aged father kept a small riverside tavern outside Jiankang, supporting each other by selling food and wine. Though a tavern keeper, he admired the martial world, enjoyed weapons practice, and eagerly befriended passing heroes, showing something of a chivalrous spirit. His path to Liangshan was linked to Yang Xiong the Sick Guan Suo, Shi Xiu the Reckless Third Son, and Dai Zong the Magic Traveler; the more immediate connection was the episode of treating An Daoquan after he had been struck by a poisoned arrow. At that time Song Jiang had developed a malignant sore on his back and was close to death. Only the Divine Physician An Daoquan, far away in Jiankang, could cure him. Dai Zong and Zhang Shun were ordered to fetch the doctor. Arriving at the riverside with his travel money gone and consumed by urgency, Zhang Shun came upon the Wang family's tavern. Recognizing a worthy man, Wang Dingliu generously helped him, led him to An Daoquan, and supported him along the way. But the doctor was entangled with a courtesan, Li Qiaonu, who refused to let him leave, while her other lover also obstructed them. With no apparent alternative, Zhang Shun resorted to a ruthless plan: he killed both the courtesan and her lover and blamed An Daoquan, forcing him to go to Liangshan. Throughout the affair Wang Dingliu assisted Zhang Shun and formed a deep bond with him. Afterwards Zhang Shun invited father and son to join the mountain. Wang Dingliu closed the riverside tavern and took his aged father to Liangshan Marsh.

His speed and skill with spear and staff earned him duties gathering intelligence and carrying military messages alongside the other swift-footed heroes. At the great ranking he took the 104th seat as the Earthly Inferior Star. He handled incoming and outgoing intelligence and various reception and support tasks. His fast feet were a rare asset: whenever urgent military news had to be carried in all directions, he was one of the army's reliable runners. The novel devotes little space to him, but he frequently appears on reconnaissance, message-bearing, and support duties, a capable swift-footed officer of Liangshan's infantry.

After the amnesty, Wang Dingliu followed the army north against Great Liao, then against Tian Hu and Wang Qing, and finally south against Fang La. Jiangnan's dangerous mountains and waters and Fang La's many fierce generals and elite troops brought appalling casualties, staining the southeast with the heroes' blood. Wang Dingliu died in this terrible campaign. During the assault on Changzhou, he fought bravely at the front against Fang La's soldiers but was outnumbered and killed in the confused fighting beneath the city walls. The Living Lightning, whose feet had carried him like a flash, could not run clear of death. He fell in Jiangnan's flames of war, another Liangshan hero sacrificed to the great undertaking of amnesty. The small Jiankang tavern where father and son had supported each other, and the hot-tempered wine seller with wind beneath his feet, faded amid the blades and spears that scattered the brotherhood in Fang La's campaign. Only his nickname remains to recall the loyalty and warm heart with which he once helped Zhang Shun fetch a physician from far away.
王定六者，建康人氏，水浒一百单八将中一员脚力极健、来去如飞的好汉。其人在江边卖酒.ja:
王定六は建康の出身で、水滸百八将の中でも脚力が非常に強く、飛ぶように往来する好漢だった。川辺で酒を売って暮らし、槍棒を習い、拳脚にも優れていた。生来たいへんせっかちで、何をするにも慌ただしく、歩けば両足から風が起こるように速かった。江湖の人々はその足の速さを見て「活閃婆」と呼んだ。「閃」は電光、「活閃」は江南の俗語で稲妻をいい、「婆」はその速さが雷電の一閃のようであることを表す添え言葉である。すなわち電光のように走る足技を称えた名で、さほど勇ましい響きではなくとも、彼の俊足をありありと表していた。

家柄も商売もまったく堅実で、老父とともに建康城外の川辺で小さな居酒屋を開き、親子で助け合いながら酒食を売って暮らしていた。酒売りを生業としながら江湖に憧れ、槍棒を好んで習い、通りかかる好漢には話しかけて親しくなろうとする侠気もあった。梁山入りの因由は病関索楊雄、拼命三郎石秀、神行太保戴宗らに結びつき、より直接には、毒矢を受けた安道全を治療する一節に関わっている。当時、梁山の宋江は背に悪い腫れ物ができて命が危うく、遠い建康にいる神医安道全でなければ治せなかった。戴宗と張順は命を受けて下山し、医師を迎えに向かった。張順が川辺へ着くと、路銀は尽き、心は焦りきっていたが、王定六父子の居酒屋に出会った。王定六は好漢と見て惜しまず助け、安道全を探す案内をし、道々世話をした。ところが安道全は妓女李巧奴に執着しており、彼女は医師を行かせようとせず、別の情夫も妨げた。張順はやむなく苛烈な策を用い、妓女と情夫を殺して安道全の仕業に見せかけ、山へ同行するほかないように追い込んだ。この騒動の始めから終わりまで王定六は張順に力を貸し、深い情を結んだ。事が済むと張順に父子そろっての入山を勧められ、王定六は川辺の店を畳み、老父を奉じて梁山泊へ向かった。

入山すると、足が速く槍棒にも慣れていたため、ほかの健脚の好漢とともに、情報の収集や軍情の伝達を専ら任された。大聚義で席次が定まり、王定六は第百四位、地劣星となり、梁山泊に出入りする情報の探索や、各種の出迎え、支援を掌った。俊足は軍中で得難い役に立ち、急報があれば各地へ走って知らせる有力な一人だった。原作での記述は多くないが、偵察、伝令、援護の任にはよく姿を見せる、歩軍の確かな俊足の働き手である。

招安後は大軍と南北を転戦し、大遼を北征し、田虎、王慶を掃討した後、方臘を討つため南へ進んだ。江南の山水は険しく、方臘の配下にも勇将と精兵が多く、梁山の好漢は惨重な死傷を出して東南の地を血で染めた。王定六もこの苛烈な征討の中で命を落とした。常州を攻め、方臘軍と戦った時、勇んで先頭に立ったが、多勢に敵せず乱軍の中で倒れ、常州城下に戦死したのである。稲妻のように走る活閃婆も、その速い足で死地を逃れることはできず、江南の戦火に倒れ、多くの梁山の好漢と同じく招安の大業の犠牲となった。建康の川辺で父子が寄り添った小さな居酒屋も、せっかちで足に風を生む酒売りも、梁山の離散とともに方臘征討の刀槍の間へ消えていった。ただ「活閃婆」の三字が、かつて張順を助けて千里の医師招請に奔走した義気と熱い心を、後人に偲ばせるのである。

王英，绰号「矮脚虎」，两淮人氏。其人身材短矮，五短身躯，然性如烈火，膂力过人，惯.en:
Wang Ying, nicknamed “Stumpy Tiger,” came from the Lianghuai region. Short in stature and limb, he nevertheless had a fiery nature and extraordinary strength. He habitually fought with two steel sabers and possessed some battlefield ability. His small size combined with fierce, agile movements made him seem a tiger on short legs, giving him his name. Originally a carter who transported goods for a living, he was tempted by a merchant's wealth during a journey, robbed him, and committed murder. Arrested and sentenced to tattooing and military exile, he escaped along the road and became a bandit at Qingfeng Mountain with Yan Shun and Zheng Tianshou, raiding homes and robbing passing merchants.

Among Qingfeng's three chiefs, Yan Shun ranked first, Wang Ying second, and Zheng Tianshou third. Wang Ying had a notorious weakness for lust: whenever he saw an attractive woman, he could scarcely restrain his wish to possess her. One day the bandits captured a sedan chair carrying the wife of Liu Gao, the official in charge of Qingfeng Fort. Delighted by her looks, Wang Ying wanted to keep her as his wife, openly displaying his eagerness. At that same time, Song Jiang, fleeing after killing Yan Poxi, passed through Qingfeng Mountain and was also captured. He narrowly escaped having his heart and liver cut out for a sobering broth when Yan Shun recognized him, rescued him, and honored him as a guest. Seeing Wang Ying's intention to seize Liu Gao's wife, Song Jiang feared trouble from detaining an official's family member and urged him to release her. Out of regard for Song Jiang, Wang Ying reluctantly agreed. The woman proved wicked and ungrateful: after returning home, she accused Song Jiang of leading the Qingfeng bandits, nearly bringing disaster upon him. That belonged to the events that followed. To satisfy Wang Ying, Song Jiang promised to find him a good wife someday, a promise he remembered.

Later, Song Jiang, Hua Rong, and their companions threw Qingfeng Fort into turmoil and fought government troops. The Qingfeng Mountain band and Hua Rong's forces all went to join Liangshan, with Wang Ying, Yan Shun, and Zheng Tianshou among them. During Liangshan's three attacks on Zhu Family Village, Wang Ying was sent into battle. Among the defenders was Hu Sanniang, the daughter of Old Master Hu of Hu Family Village, nicknamed One-Zhang Green. She rode a dark-maned horse, wielded twin Sun and Moon sabers, and was highly skilled. At the sight of this beautiful woman warrior, Wang Ying's old weakness returned. Distracted by desire, he advanced with his blades to capture her alive. His ordinary skill and wandering attention could not sustain even a few exchanges. Hu Sanniang feigned an opening, turned her horse, and struck; he could not withstand her. Parting her two blades, she seized him alive and hauled him onto her horse. His lust had made him the captive of a woman warrior and a laughingstock. Lin Chong later captured Hu Sanniang and sent her to the mountain. Remembering his promise, Song Jiang arranged her marriage to Wang Ying, fulfilling his long-held desire and forming a Liangshan match. The two became husband and wife and served together in the brotherhood.

At the great ranking of the 108, Wang Ying answered to the Earthly Minute Star and held the fifty-eighth seat among the Earthly Stars. He and Hu Sanniang oversaw infantry officers and often went into battle together, making an effective mounted pair. Though his martial skill was not exceptional, he could still contribute in action and frequently charged beside his wife.

After Song Jiang accepted amnesty, Wang Ying campaigned against Great Liao, Tian Hu, Wang Qing, and Fang La, always with Hu Sanniang. In the Fang La campaign the army reached Muzhou. Fang La then had the formidable general Zheng Biao and the sorcerous National Preceptor Bao Daoyi in his service. Wang Ying rode out to fight Zheng Biao but could not match his skill. Zheng Biao pierced him with a spear, and he fell dead from his horse. Seeing her husband killed, Hu Sanniang charged to help in grief and fury. Zheng Biao used sorcery against her, sending an object flying into her face. Caught unprepared, she too died before the armies. Husband and wife gave their lives on the same day beneath Muzhou's walls, united in marriage and sharing life and death, a tragic martial union in Water Margin. The Stumpy Tiger, who had lusted all his life and gained a beautiful wife, finally went with her to the underworld before the army returned or he could receive honors: a sorrowful fate.
王英，绰号「矮脚虎」，两淮人氏。其人身材短矮，五短身躯，然性如烈火，膂力过人，惯.ja:
王英は「矮脚虎」の異名を持つ両淮の出身者である。背も手足も短かったが、気性は烈火のようで腕力は人に優れ、二振りの鋼刀を使って戦場でも相応の働きをした。丈は低くとも動きは凶猛で素早く、短い脚の虎のようだったので、江湖で「矮脚虎」と呼ばれた。もとは車を引いて荷を運ぶ車夫だったが、道中で財に心を動かされ、商人の金品を奪って人を殺した。捕らえられて入墨と軍への流刑に処されたものの、護送中に逃れ、清風山で山賊となった。燕順、鄭天寿と山を占め、家々を襲い、通行する商人を略奪した。

清風山の三頭領では燕順が首位、王英が第二位、鄭天寿が末席だった。王英には色欲が甚だしいという欠点があり、美しい婦人を見るたびに自分のものにしたくてたまらなくなることを、山寨中が知っていた。ある日、手下が捕らえた駕籠に、清風寨の知寨劉高の妻が乗っていた。見目のよさに王英は喜び、山に留めて妻にしようと、せっかちな欲望をあらわにした。折しも閻婆惜を殺して難を避ける宋江も清風山を通り、手下に捕らえられ、あやうく酔い覚ましの汁にするため心肝をえぐられるところだった。燕順が宋江と気づいて慌てて救い、上客として迎えた。王英が劉高の妻を無理に占有しようとするのを見た宋江は、命官の家族だけに騒ぎを恐れ、放すよう勧めた。王英は宋江の顔を立て、惜しみながらも返した。ところが女は恩知らずの悪女で、帰ると宋江を清風山の賊首だと偽って訴え、彼を幾度も災難に遭わせた。それは後の話である。宋江は王英の好色を見て、いずれよい妻を探すと約束し、王英はその言葉を覚えていた。

後に宋江、花栄らが清風寨を騒がせ、官軍と戦うと、清風山の一党と花栄らの軍勢は皆、梁山泊へ向かった。王英、燕順、鄭天寿も共に入山した。梁山が三度祝家荘を攻めた際、王英は命を受けて出戦した。敵方には扈家荘の扈太公の娘、扈三娘という「一丈青」の女将がいた。日月双刀を使い、青いたてがみの馬に乗る、武芸に優れた人物だった。美しい女将を見た王英は悪癖を再発させ、色に心を奪われて戦いを忘れ、刀を構えて生け捕りにしようと進んだ。もとより腕は並で、美色にも気を取られていたため、数合も持たなかった。扈三娘が隙を見せて馬を返し、一刀を放つと防ぎきれない。彼女は双刀を左右に分けて王英を生け捕りにし、馬上へさらった。好色が災いして女将の捕虜となり、笑いものになったのである。後に林冲が扈三娘を捕らえて山へ送ると、宋江は以前の約束を忘れず、彼女を王英の妻にすると決めた。王英の長年の願いがかなうとともに梁山の一組の縁が成り、以後二人は夫婦として仲間に列した。

大聚義で百八将の席次が定まると、王英は地微星に応じ、地煞の第五十八位となった。妻の扈三娘と歩軍の将校を司り、しばしば組んで出戦し、夫婦の二騎はよく補い合った。王英の武芸はそれほど高くなくとも、陣中で役に立ち、たびたび三娘と肩を並べて突撃した。

宋江が招安を受けると、王英は大軍に従って大遼を北征し、田虎、王慶を討ち、さらに方臘を征したが、いつも扈三娘と一緒だった。方臘征討で軍は睦州に至った。当時、敵方には勇将鄭彪がおり、妖術を使う国師包道乙もいた。王英は馬を進めて鄭彪と戦ったが、その技にはかなわず、一槍を受けて落馬し、陣中に死んだ。後方で夫の死を見た扈三娘は、悲しみと怒りに駆られて救いに駆けたが、鄭彪の妖術に傷つけられた。飛来した物が顔を直撃し、不意を突かれた彼女も陣前に倒れた。夫婦は同じ日に命を捧げ、そろって睦州城下に戦死した。髪を結んで心を一つにし、生死を共にした、水滸の壮烈な婚姻の一節である。生涯色を貪り、美しい妻を得た矮脚虎も、最後は妻と共に黄泉へ赴き、凱旋にも封賞にも届かなかった。痛ましく悲しい結末である。

魏定国，凌州人氏，原系大宋凌州团练使，与同郡单廷珪并为凌州二将，素来交厚，情同骨.en:
Wei Dingguo, a native of Lingzhou, was originally the Song dynasty's militia training commissioner there. He and Shan Tinggui of the same prefecture were known as the Two Generals of Lingzhou, close friends who felt like flesh and blood. An expert in fire attacks, Wei Dingguo could use fire cannon, fire arrows, fire beasts, and other incendiary devices with equal skill. He burned camps and strongholds and shattered enemy formations with flames. Soldiers said he could command fire itself, earning him the imposing nickname “General of Divine Fire.” Among Liangshan Marsh's 108 heroes, he answered to the Earthly Fierce Star, held the forty-fifth seat, and served as a junior cavalry commander and leader of long-range scouts. Shan Tinggui mastered water and Wei Dingguo fire: their complementary arts made them a rare pair of remarkable generals in Liangshan's army.

Like Shan Tinggui, he came to Liangshan through the campaign led by Guan Sheng, the Great Saber. When Liangshan attacked Daming Prefecture and shook Hebei, Grand Preceptor Cai recommended Guan Sheng to lead the suppression force. Guan Sheng requested Lingzhou's two militia commissioners, Shan Tinggui and Wei Dingguo, as his wings, hoping water attacks and fire attacks would overcome Liangshan's advantage as a marsh stronghold. Yet on reaching Liangshan, Guan Sheng fell into Song Jiang's trap, was captured, and joined the brotherhood after being moved by its loyalty. Song Jiang admired the two Lingzhou generals' talents and sent the newly surrendered Guan Sheng to recruit them.

Guan Sheng advanced on Lingzhou and first captured Shan Tinggui, who had come out to fight. After Shan Tinggui submitted, Wei Dingguo remained alone to defend the city. Hearing of his friend's surrender and seeing Guan Sheng at the walls, he hesitated. Guan Sheng knew that he valued loyalty and chose not to storm the city. Instead he rode alone to its gates and sincerely invited him to join, explaining Song Jiang's desire to carry out Heaven's justice and his generous treatment of worthy men. Shan Tinggui also pleaded earnestly on Liangshan's behalf. Wei Dingguo saw Guan Sheng's complete sincerity and remembered his lifelong bond with Shan Tinggui. If his sworn friend had gone to the mountain, how could he remain behind alone? He opened the gates, welcomed Guan Sheng, agreed to submit, and accompanied both men to Liangshan. With the two Lingzhou generals standing together beneath the Hall of Brotherhood, Liangshan's prestige grew further.

Once at Liangshan, Wei Dingguo campaigned north and south, his fire attacks proving especially powerful in storming cities and breaking formations. His troops carried fire cannon, fire arrows, and other incendiary gear. They set enemy camps ablaze and charged when the flames threw the defenders into disorder, repeatedly taking cities and forts. He and Shan Tinggui supported each other with water and fire, one trapping the enemy and the other burning them, earning the Two Generals of Lingzhou still greater renown. At the great ranking, Wei Dingguo joined the Earthly Stars and took responsibility for cavalry vanguard and scouting duties, his reputation undiminished. His incendiaries burned and drove back enemies, showing him a fierce and seasoned fighting general. Whenever the army marched, he and Shan Tinggui led a force together; the appearance of the Water and Fire Generals filled enemies with dread.

After the imperial amnesty, Wei Dingguo fought under Song Jiang against Great Liao, Tian Hu in Hebei, and Wang Qing in Huaixi. He won repeated honors across the land and upheld the name General of Divine Fire. Then came the Jiangnan campaign against Fang La, where more than half Liangshan's heroes fell, including Wei Dingguo. As the army besieged Shezhou, defenders used the difficult terrain to resist desperately, and battle followed battle beneath the walls amid showers of arrows and stones. Wei Dingguo bravely attacked, but an unexpected enemy rush in the confused fighting overtook him, and he died fighting hard beneath Shezhou's walls. Shan Tinggui, his friend in life and death, perished in the same campaign. They had sought loyalty and fulfilled it, remaining together through death and honoring their lifelong bond. The famous fire specialist of Lingzhou had gone from militia commissioner to Liangshan commander and fought north and south, only to end with his body wrapped in horsehide and his blood on the battlefield. After Song Jiang defeated Fang La and returned, the court honored the fallen. Wei Dingguo received the posthumous title Zhongwulang, and his spirit returned to his homeland. His command of fire, sincere allegiance, and friendship with Shan Tinggui remain a celebrated, sorrowful tale of Liangshan.
魏定国，凌州人氏，原系大宋凌州团练使，与同郡单廷珪并为凌州二将，素来交厚，情同骨.ja:
魏定国は凌州の出身で、もとは大宋の凌州団練使だった。同郡の単廷珪と「凌州の二将」と称され、かねて親しく、骨肉のような情を結んでいた。火攻めに精通し、火砲、火箭、火獣などの火器を自在に用い、烈火で陣営や寨を焼き、敵陣を崩して鋭鋒を砕いた。軍中では火勢を使役し、神火に号令できると噂され、「神火将」という赫々たる異名を得た。梁山泊百八人の中では地猛星に応じ、第四十五位に座し、馬軍小彪将兼遠探出哨頭領を務めた。単廷珪は水、魏定国は火に長じ、水火が助け合って一軍を成す、梁山でも得難い奇将の一組だった。

梁山入りの因由は単廷珪と同じく、「大刀」関勝による梁山征討に始まる。梁山の好漢が大名府を攻めて河北を騒がせると、蔡太師は関勝を推挙して討伐を率いさせた。関勝は凌州団練使の単廷珪と魏定国を左右の翼として求め、水攻めと火攻めで梁山水寨の利を制そうとした。ところが関勝は梁山に迫ると宋江の計略にはまり、捕らえられて山へ送られ、義に感じて帰順した。二将の才を愛した宋江は、降った関勝に、自ら凌州へ行って招くよう命じた。

関勝は兵を率いて凌州へ向かい、まず出戦した単廷珪を捕らえた。単廷珪が帰順すると、城を守るのは魏定国一人となった。友の降伏を知り、関勝の軍が城下へ来たのを見て、心は揺れた。魏定国が義を重んじると知る関勝は強攻を望まず、単身一騎で城下へ赴き、誠意をもって招いた。宋公明が天に代わって道を行い、義を尊び財を惜しまない心を詳しく語り、単廷珪も傍らで懸命に梁山の義を説いた。関勝が腹を割って語る姿と、単廷珪との生死を共にする交わりを思い、友が帰山した以上、自分だけ残ることができようかと考えた。ついに城門を開いて関勝を迎え、帰順を願い、二人と共に梁山へ上った。凌州の二将はそろって仲間となり、水火の将が聚義庁に並んで、梁山の威勢はいっそう増した。

入山後、魏定国は大軍と南北を転戦し、攻城や敵陣突破の際に火攻めの威力を発揮した。配下は火砲、火箭などの火具を多く備え、戦えば烈火で敵営を焼き、敵陣が乱れると兵を駆って攻め込み、城や寨の攻略に力を示した。単廷珪と左右に呼応し、水で敵を封じ、火で焼く、互いに補う一組の奇将として、凌州二将の名はますます広まった。大聚義では地煞に列し、馬軍の先鋒と偵察を担い、往年に劣らぬ威名を保った。火器で敵を焼き退ける、戦慣れた勇将である。遠征のたびに単廷珪と一軍を率い、水火の二将がそろって出れば、敵はその名を聞いて胆を冷やした。

朝廷の招安後、魏定国は宋江に従い、まず大遼を破り、次いで河北の田虎、淮西の王慶を平定した。各地を転戦して幾度も功を立て、「神火将」の名を落とさなかった。しかし江南の方臘征討では梁山の好漢が半数以上を失い、彼も戦没した。歙州を囲む大軍に対し、敵将は険地を頼みに死守し、城下では矢石が雨のように降る激戦が続いた。魏定国は勇んで城を攻めたが、敵と戦う最中に乱軍から不意に突きかかられ、城下で力戦して命を落とした。生死の友、単廷珪も同じ戦役に死んだ。仁を求めて仁を得たといえ、死にも連れ添い、生涯の交わりに背かなかった。火攻めを得意として凌州に名を轟かせた神火将は、団練使から梁山へ帰順し、南北を戦った末、軍馬の革に遺体を包まれ、戦場に血を流す最期となった。宋江が方臘を平定して凱旋すると、朝廷は戦没将佐を追封し、魏定国にも忠武郎が贈られ、魂は故郷へ帰った。その火攻めの才、帰義の誠、単廷珪と生死を共にした友情は、梁山の無念に満ちた佳話として今も語られる。

武松者，清河县人氏，排行第二，江湖上人称「武二郎」。其人身长八尺，浑身上下有千百.en:
Wu Song was a native of Qinghe County and the second son of his family, known in the martial world as Wu Erlang. Eight chi tall, with the strength of hundreds or thousands of jin throughout his body, he had bold features and an imposing appearance. Later, at Crossroads Slope, Zhang Qing and Sun Erniang gave him an ascetic's ordination certificate, monastic sabers, and black cloth robe. Disguised as a traveling religious practitioner, he became known as “Wu Song the Pilgrim.”

In his early years, a drunken quarrel left him believing that he had killed a man. He fled to Chai Jin's estate and sheltered there for more than a year. Song Jiang was also staying there; impressed by Wu Song's uncommon bearing, he became his sworn brother. Learning that the man back home had survived, Wu Song took leave of Chai Jin and Song Jiang to visit his elder brother Wu Da in Qinghe. At Jingyang Ridge in Yanggu County, a tavern's sign warned, “After three bowls, do not cross the ridge.” Wu Song drank eighteen and climbed the ridge in high spirits. Near dusk, a white-browed tiger with slanting eyes sprang out. He dodged its pounce, lift, and tail sweep, then struck with his staff, only to break it against a tree. In desperation he seized the tiger's striped head with bare hands, pinned it to the ground, and pounded it with all his strength until it died. The tiger-killing at Jingyang Ridge made his name throughout the land, and Yanggu's magistrate appointed him infantry constable.

In Yanggu he reunited with Wu Da, a timid, short man married to the seductively beautiful Pan Jinlian. Attracted by Wu Song's powerful build, she tried to seduce him, but he firmly rejected her. She later committed adultery with Ximen Qing, and together they poisoned Wu Da with arsenic. Returning from official business, Wu Song suspected that his brother's death was unnatural. He gathered evidence and appealed to the authorities, but his complaint was rejected. He then took vengeance himself: before his brother's memorial tablet he killed Pan Jinlian, cut open her body, and offered her heart to the dead. He went to Lion Tower and fought Ximen Qing, killing him below the building. Rather than flee, he carried their severed heads to the authorities and surrendered with his own hands bound, acting openly. Because his crimes had cause, he escaped execution and was tattooed and exiled to Mengzhou.

There he met Shi En, the prison superintendent's son. Shi En's Happy Forest tavern had been seized by the bully Jiang the Door God under Militia Commissioner Zhang's protection. Grateful for Shi En's kindness, Wu Song intervened. On his way he drank at every tavern, passing none without taking three bowls. In the famous drunken beating, he thrashed Jiang until the bully knelt and begged, recovering Happy Forest. Jiang then conspired with Commandant Zhang and Militia Commissioner Zhang to frame Wu Song for theft and have him killed at Flying Cloud Pool. Wu Song broke free of his restraints and killed the two escort officers and two assassins instead. Burning with rage, he returned that night to the commandant's residence. In the bloodbath at Mandarin Duck Tower, he killed the two Zhangs, Jiang, and all the men and women in the household. Dipping his hand in blood, he wrote on the wall, “The killer is Wu Song, the tiger slayer.” His ferocious resolve reached its extreme there.

With nowhere left to go, he was helped by Zhang Qing and Sun Erniang, who disguised him as a pilgrim and sent him toward Twin Dragons Mountain. Along the way, he crossed Centipede Ridge at night and killed the wicked Daoist called the Flying Centipede. At Twin Dragons Mountain he joined Lu Zhishen and Yang Zhi. After the three mountain bands attacked Qingzhou, they all went to Liangshan. At the great assembly, Wu Song ranked fourteenth among the Heavenly Stars as the Heavenly Wounded Star. He shared command of the infantry with Lu Zhishen and was regarded as one of Liangshan's toughest infantry generals. Famous for his two monastic sabers and skilled with fists and feet, he could kill a tiger barehanded and overpower bands of villains with matchless ferocity.

After the amnesty, Wu Song campaigned against Liao and Fang La. While fighting rebel officers at Black Dragon Ridge in the Fang La campaign, the sorcerer Bao Daoyi secretly sent a flying sword that severed his left arm. Enduring the pain, Wu Song struck back with his monastic saber and cut Bao Daoyi down, but was left disabled. On the return journey, Song Jiang intended to bring the commanders to the capital for honors. Wu Song, his heart grown cold, declined: “I am disabled now and do not wish to attend court. I hope to enter religious life here.” He became a monk at Liuhe Temple and spent his remaining years there, dying peacefully at eighty. A fierce hero who had repaid kindness and vengeance decisively for half his life ended with a lost arm, a monk's vows, and the quiet company of an oil lamp and the Buddha: one of Water Margin's deeply sorrowful final refuges.
武松者，清河县人氏，排行第二，江湖上人称「武二郎」。其人身长八尺，浑身上下有千百.ja:
武松は清河県の出身で、兄弟の二番目に当たり、江湖では「武二郎」と呼ばれた。身の丈八尺、全身に千百斤もの力を備え、眉目は雄々しく、堂々たる容姿だった。後に十字坡の張青、孫二娘の所で頭陀の度牒、戒刀、黒布の直裰を得て行者に扮し、以後「行者武松」と呼ばれるようになった。

若い頃、酔って人と争い、殺してしまったと思い込んで柴進の荘園へ逃れ、一年以上身を隠した。その間、同じく滞在していた宋江と知り合い、非凡な風貌を認められて義兄弟となった。やがて故郷の相手が死んでいないと聞き、柴進と宋江に別れを告げ、兄の武大を訪ねて清河へ帰ろうとした。陽谷県の景陽岡では、麓の居酒屋の旗に「三碗飲めば岡を越せぬ」とあったが、武松は十八碗も飲み、酒興に乗って岡へ上った。夕暮れ時、吊り上がった目と白い額の大虎が飛び出した。武松は飛びかかり、跳ね上げ、尾の払いの三つの攻撃をかわし、棒を振るったが、木に当たって折れてしまう。窮した彼は素手で虎の頭の斑皮をつかみ、地に押さえつけ、力いっぱい拳を浴びせて殴り殺した。この「景陽岡の虎退治」で天下に名が轟き、陽谷知県は県の歩兵都頭に取り立てた。

陽谷では兄の武大と再会した。小柄で気の弱い武大には、妖艶な妻の潘金蓮がいた。武松のたくましさに惹かれた彼女は誘惑したが、厳しく拒まれた。後に西門慶と通じ、二人で謀って砒素で武大を毒殺した。公務から戻った武松は兄の死を怪しみ、証拠を集めて訴えたが受理されず、自ら決着をつけた。まず霊前で潘金蓮を斬り、腹を裂いて心臓を取り、兄に供えた。続いて獅子楼へ向かい、西門慶と戦って楼下で殺した。殺人後も逃げ隠れせず、二人の首を持ち、自ら縛られて役所へ出頭するほど公然としていた。事情があったため死刑は免れ、入墨を受けて孟州へ流された。

孟州では管営の息子、施恩と知り合った。施恩の「快活林」という居酒屋は、張団練の勢力を頼む悪漢の蔣門神に奪われていた。厚いもてなしに感じた武松は助力を引き受けた。その日は道中で、酒旗のある店を三碗飲まずには通らないという調子で酒を重ね、酔いに乗じて蔣門神を打ち、膝をついて命乞いさせ、快活林を取り戻した。恨んだ蔣門神は張都監、張団練と結託し、武松を盗みの罪に陥れ、飛雲浦で殺そうとした。武松は枷を脱し、逆に二人の護送役と二人の刺客を殺した。怒りに燃えてその夜都監の屋敷へ戻り、「鴛鴦楼に血を飛ばす」惨劇で張都監、張団練、蔣門神と屋敷の男女を皆殺しにした。血をつけて壁に「人を殺したのは虎退治の武松なり」と大書し、その激烈で決然とした気性はここに極まった。

行き場を失った武松は、張青と孫二娘に行者へ変装させてもらい、二竜山へ向かった。途中、夜に蜈蚣嶺を越え、悪を働く飛天蜈蚣の道人を斬った。二竜山では魯智深、楊志と義を結び、後に三山が青州を攻めると、皆で梁山へ帰順した。大聚義では天罡第十四位の「天傷星」となり、魯智深と歩軍を掌り、梁山の歩将でも第一級の剛の者とされた。二振りの戒刀で名高く、拳脚にも通じ、素手で虎を打ち、群がる凶漢を力で倒す剛猛さは並ぶものがなかった。

招安後は遼国と方臘の征討に従った。方臘との戦いで烏竜嶺の賊将と戦っていた際、妖人包道乙が密かに飛剣を放ち、左腕を斬り落とされた。武松は激痛に耐えて戒刀を返し、包道乙を斬り倒したが、以後は片腕の身となった。凱旋の途中、宋江が諸将を都へ連れて行き封賞を受けさせようとすると、心の冷えた武松は「今はこの不自由な身です。都へ参内することは望まず、ここで出家したい」と辞退した。六和寺で出家して余生を送り、八十歳で安らかに没した。半生を痛快な恩讐の決着に生き、火のように激しかった好漢が、腕を失い、青い灯と古仏を友として生涯を閉じたのは、水滸の中でも深いため息を誘う帰結である。

吴用，字学究，道号加亮先生，绰号「智多星」。其乃山东济州郓城县东溪村人氏，与晁盖.en:
Wu Yong, courtesy name Xuejiu and Daoist name Master Jialiang, was nicknamed “Resourceful Star.” He came from Dongxi Village in Yuncheng County, Jizhou, Shandong, the same home as Chao Gai. Refined in feature, fair-faced, and long-bearded, he originally taught village children for a living and was therefore called Scholar Wu. Yet within him lay the equivalent of a million armored troops and countless ingenious plans. He understood the Six Secret Teachings and Three Strategies, mastered the interplay of yin and yang, and possessed schemes said to surpass Zhuge Kongming's, earning his nickname. Usually dressed in a Daoist robe and holding a feather fan, he could wield two copper chains. Martial prowess was not his chief gift: as Liangshan's foremost strategist, he planned victories.

His rise began with the clever seizure of the birthday gifts. Grand Secretary Liang of Daming Prefecture in the Northern Capital planned to send treasure worth one hundred thousand strings of cash to celebrate his father-in-law Cai Jing's birthday. Chao Gai learned of it and discussed robbing the shipment with Wu Yong. Wu Yong devised the plan and brought together Liu Tang, Gongsun Sheng, the three Ruan brothers, and Bai Sheng in a seven-man undertaking. At Yellow Mud Ridge they drugged Yang Zhi's escort and took the gifts. His first display of strategy achieved a great success, and the seven stars' gathering became a celebrated tale. When the crime was exposed, he fled to Liangshan with Chao Gai and the others. Wang Lun, then chief, was too narrow-minded to welcome worthy men. Wu Yong secretly provoked Lin Chong into killing him and installed Chao Gai as leader. Liangshan took on a new character, and Wu Yong became its strategist.

As strategist he planned Liangshan's campaigns, great and small. In the three attacks on Zhu Family Village, he overcame the maze of paths and had Sun Li feign surrender as an inside agent. A coordinated attack then broke the village. He also planned Lu Junyi's recruitment: disguised as a fortune teller, he wrote a rebellious poem on a wall and drew the Northern Capital's Jade Qilin into his trap. Tricking the Jade Qilin, taking Daming, luring Guan Sheng, capturing Dong Ping, taking Huazhou, and bringing Xu Ning to the mountain to defeat the linked cavalry, as well as the schemes involving Zhu Tong, Qin Ming, and Xu Ning, all displayed his ingenuity. Deception was his specialty, and he preferred winning minds to relying on brute force. Liangshan repeatedly defeated larger armies, with Wu Yong making the greatest contribution.

After Chao Gai's death, Wu Yong strongly supported Song Jiang as chief. United with him, he offered comprehensive counsel, arranged the rankings, and shared military and administrative responsibilities. When all 108 heroes assembled, Wu Yong held the third seat as the Heavenly Secret Star. He served as chief strategist for confidential military affairs and managed the army with Gongsun Sheng, becoming Song Jiang's trusted right hand. The two victories over Tong Guan and three defeats of Gao Qiu depended on his formations, ambushes, and feints, which repeatedly routed the court's armies.

He had doubts about amnesty, fearing that the court could not tolerate them, but ultimately followed Song Jiang into submission. In the Liao campaign he offered many plans and helped break the Celestial Configuration Formation. Against Tian Hu and Wang Qing, he served as adviser, planning from headquarters and helping Lu Junyi and Song Jiang pacify both regions. In the southern campaign against Fang La, he exhausted his efforts directing commanders through Jiangnan's difficult terrain. Yet more than half the Liangshan brothers fell, and even he could not reverse their fate. He could only watch their ranks dwindle in grief.

After Fang La's defeat, the court appointed him military commissioner of Wusheng Army. Long experience had taught him that wicked ministers ruled affairs and that Song Jiang and Lu Junyi were unlikely to find peaceful ends. When he heard that Song Jiang and Li Kui had died of poisoning and been buried at Liao'er Marsh in Chuzhou, grief overwhelmed him. One night he dreamed that they called to him and told him of their unjust deaths. Awakening with a heart cut by sorrow, he went straight to Song Jiang's grave. Hua Rong had also arrived. Both felt the weight of Song Jiang's kindness, the sorrow of the brothers' dispersal, and the uncertainty of the world. They agreed to die together and hanged themselves from a tree before the grave, preserving the bond of leader and followers, brothers in loyalty. They were buried beside Song Jiang at Liao'er Marsh so that they might remain together in death.

Throughout his life, Wu Yong was resourceful and full of plans. From Yellow Mud Ridge to Liangshan's great assembly, amnesty, and campaigns, no major undertaking lacked his counsel. Though he did not charge with spear or saber, his devotion and learning built Liangshan's cause, making him Water Margin's foremost man of wisdom. Yet even the wise could not defy destiny. He saw the loyal brotherhood perish and finally gave his own life for Song Jiang. When Emperor Huizong later granted posthumous honors to Liangshan's commanders, Wu Yong was among them. The Resourceful Star's name and strategic achievements passed down with the brotherhood's deeds of loyalty to enduring fame.
吴用，字学究，道号加亮先生，绰号「智多星」。其乃山东济州郓城县东溪村人氏，与晁盖.ja:
呉用は字を学究、道号を加亮先生といい、「智多星」の異名を持つ。山東済州の鄆城県東渓村の出身で、晁蓋と同郷だった。眉目秀麗で顔は白く、髭は長く、もとは村の子供を教える学究だったため、呉学究と呼ばれた。しかし胸中には百万の甲兵と神機妙算を秘め、六韜三略に通じ、陰陽を使いこなし、諸葛孔明にも勝る知略を持つとされ、江湖で智多星の名を得た。普段は羽扇を振り、道袍を着け、二本の銅鎖を使った。武勇を主とする人物ではないが、策をめぐらして勝敗を決する梁山第一の謀主であった。

入山の発端は、生辰綱を知略で奪ったことである。北京大名府の梁中書は、岳父蔡京の誕生日を祝うため、十万貫の金珠宝物を生辰綱として送ろうとした。これを聞いた晁蓋が呉用に奪取を相談すると、呉用は妙計を定め、劉唐、公孫勝、阮氏三雄、白勝を誘った七人で、黄泥岡において眠り薬で楊志一行を倒し、生辰綱を奪った。初めて知略を試して大事を成し、七星聚義は佳話となった。事件が発覚すると、晁蓋らと梁山へ上った。当時の王倫は狭量で豪傑を容れなかったため、呉用は密かに林冲を刺激して王倫を討たせ、晁蓋を頭領に据えた。梁山の気風は一新され、呉用は軍師の職を掌った。

軍師として、梁山の大小の戦いはすべて彼の計画に基づいた。三度の祝家荘攻めでは、入り組む盤陀路を策で破り、孫立を偽降させて内応役とし、内外から呼応して祝家を攻略した。盧俊義を山へ誘うのも彼の策で、占い師に扮して壁に反詩を書き、北京の玉麒麟を罠にかけた。玉麒麟を招き、大名府を取り、関勝を誘い、董平を捕らえ、華州を奪い、徐寧を山へ招いて連環馬を破ること、さらに朱仝、秦明、徐寧を誘い込むことなど、一つ一つに神機が見られる。その策は相手を「計って誘う」ことを得意とし、心を攻めるのを上策として、腕力だけには頼らなかった。梁山が少数で多数に勝つことが多かったのは、呉用の功が最も大きい。

晁蓋の死後、呉用は宋江を山寨の主にと強く推した。宋江と心を合わせて周到に補佐し、席次を決め、軍政を分掌した。百八将の聚義では天機星、第三位に座し、機密軍師として公孫勝と軍務を理し、宋江の股肱となった。童貫を二度破り、高俅を三度敗ったのも、呉用が陣法を指揮し、伏兵や疑惑を仕掛け、朝廷の大軍を繰り返し敗走させたためである。

招安には疑念があり、朝廷が自分たちを容れないことを恐れたが、結局は宋江と共に帰順した。招安後は遼国征討で多くの策を献じ、混天象陣を破った。田虎、王慶の征討では参謀として帷幄に策をめぐらし、盧俊義と宋江による両地の平定を助けた。方臘への南征では、険しい江南で心血を注いで諸将を配置した。しかし梁山の兄弟は半数以上を失い、呉用にも運命を覆す力はなく、ただ仲間の零落を見て悲しむばかりだった。

方臘平定後、朝廷から武勝軍承宣使に任じられた。しかし世の事情を長く見てきた彼は、奸臣が権勢を握る以上、宋江と盧俊義が安らかな終わりを得るのは難しいと知っていた。宋江と李逵が毒で死に、楚州の蓼児窪へ葬られたと聞くと、悲しみに耐えられなかった。ある夜、夢で二人に呼ばれ、無実の死を訴えられた。目覚めて胸をえぐられる思いとなり、まっすぐ宋江の墓へ向かった。そこには花栄も来ていた。二人は宋公明の恩義の深さを思い、兄弟の離散と世の無常を痛み、共に死ぬことを約した。宋江の墓前の木でそろって首を吊り、君臣と兄弟の義を全うした。後人は蓼児窪の宋江の墓の側に二人を葬り、生死を共にさせた。

呉用は一生、知恵と策略に富み、計算に遺漏がなかった。黄泥岡の生辰綱奪取から梁山の聚義、招安後の征戦まで、謀議に加わらぬ戦役はない。刀槍を手に突撃することはなくとも、心血と経綸を尽くして梁山の大業を成し、水滸第一の智者といえる。しかし智者も天命には逆らえず、忠義の士が共に滅ぶのを目にし、自らも宋江への義に殉じた。後に徽宗が梁山諸将を追封した際、呉用も勅封に列した。智多星の名と神機妙算の実績は、梁山の忠義の事績とともに後世へ不朽に伝わった。

项充，绰号「八臂哪吒」，应地煞地飞星，乃梁山泊一百单八将中第六十四位好汉，位列步.en:
Xiang Chong, nicknamed “Eight-Armed Nezha,” answered to the Earthly Flying Star and ranked sixty-fourth among Liangshan Marsh's 108 heroes. An infantry commander, he joined Liangshan with Li Gun and Fan Rui from Mount Mangdang. Born in Pei County, Xuzhou, he was strong and exceptionally brave, adept at handling flying shields and round shields. His usual round shield held twenty-four throwing knives, and he carried javelins behind his back. In battle he spun the shield like a windmill to protect his body while launching knives and javelins with lightning speed at enemies several paces away. His uncanny attacks swept aside resistance. With shield, knives, and spears all moving together, he seemed to possess eight arms, while his ferocity recalled Prince Nezha of legend, who had three heads and six arms and rode wind-and-fire wheels. The nickname Eight-Armed Nezha praised the variety of his techniques and speed of his movements.

He had long been close to Li Gun. Both were fugitives from the Xuzhou region who, after committing crimes and finding nowhere to stay, went to Mount Mangdang and joined Fan Rui, the sorcerous Demon King of Chaos. Fan Rui was chief and the two became his deputies. They occupied the mountain, gathered a forest band, and raided and robbed. Fan Rui could summon wind and rain, while Xiang Chong and Li Gun had exceptional shield, spear, throwing-knife, and javelin skills. Their combined strength won them such renown that they began to dream of annexing Liangshan Marsh, boasting that they would seize its stronghold. This provoked their conflict with Liangshan.

Hearing the three men's boast, Song Jiang mustered an army and personally marched against Mount Mangdang. Gongsun Sheng accompanied him, saying Fan Rui's unorthodox arts could be controlled by true magic. In battle, Xiang Chong and Li Gun led the charge, holding round shields and brandishing javelins as they rolled forward close to the ground like a whirlwind. They burst into Song Jiang's formation and drove left and right without resistance, nearly taking his life. Lu Fang and Guo Sheng saved him, thrusting out their paired painted halberds and fighting hard to block the attackers. Gongsun Sheng also secretly aided them with spells and concealed pits prepared in advance. Eager to display their courage and carried away by the fighting, Xiang Chong and Li Gun failed to watch the ground. Both fell into the pits with their shields. Hidden soldiers rushed them with hooks and ropes, captured them alive, and brought them before the command tent.

Admiring their ability, Song Jiang came out personally, sent the soldiers away, untied them, and helped them into the tent. He served wine, reassured them kindly, and explained his purpose of carrying out Heaven's justice and gathering worthy men, urging them to leave darkness for the light. The two were straightforward men. Grateful that he treated them with such kindness and courtesy instead of as prisoners, they bowed and willingly submitted. They volunteered to return to Mount Mangdang and persuade Fan Rui to join. There they recounted Song Jiang's generosity and loyalty and urged Fan Rui not to remain obsessed with magical rivalry. When Fan Rui later lost his duel with Gongsun Sheng, he recognized the superiority of the orthodox arts. Under the two friends' earnest persuasion, he led the entire Mount Mangdang force into Liangshan's ranks. The three joined the marsh together and never separated again.

At the great ranking, Xiang Chong took the sixty-fourth seat as the Earthly Flying Star, serving as an infantry commander beside Li Gun. Their round shields and throwing knives were ideally suited to charging formations and leading assaults. In the hardest battles they usually entered first and threw enemy lines into confusion, an irresistible pair of infantry vanguards. During the subsequent campaigns against Liao, Tian Hu, and Wang Qing, Xiang Chong repeatedly fought at the front and earned merit.

The Jiangnan campaign against Fang La brought the greatest danger. As the army reached the Shezhou region, Xiang Chong and Li Gun again led their troops into the enemy formation. They unexpectedly entered an ambush in treacherous terrain. Caught unprepared, they could not fully use their shields and were surrounded in the confused battle. Xiang Chong fought without retreat but was finally killed beneath many blades. The Eight-Armed Nezha, who had spent half a lifetime whirling his shield and throwing knives against every foe, lost his wings among Jiangnan's mountains. He and his dear friend Li Gun fell one after the other on the same day, never seeing the army's return. His loyal courage and terrible end form one of the most stirring passages in Water Margin's many heroic laments, leaving later readers to mourn his loss.
项充，绰号「八臂哪吒」，应地煞地飞星，乃梁山泊一百单八将中第六十四位好汉，位列步.ja:
項充は「八臂哪吒」の異名を持ち、地煞の地飛星に応じる、梁山泊百八将の第六十四位の好漢である。歩軍頭領に列し、李袞、樊瑞とともに芒碭山の一隊から梁山へ帰順した。徐州沛県の出身で、体は強健、勇猛さは並外れ、飛牌や団牌を扱う名手だった。常用する丸盾には二十四本の飛刀を差し、背には投槍も隠していた。戦場では盾を風車のように舞わせて全身を守り、電光石火の間に槍や刀を投げて数歩先の敵を傷つけた。まさに神出鬼没で、立ち塞がる者をなぎ倒した。盾が翻り、刀槍が同時に動く様子は八本の腕があるようで、三頭六臂、風火輪に乗る神話の哪吒太子のように勇猛だったため、「八臂哪吒」と呼ばれた。手段の多さと動作の速さを称える名である。

項充はもとから李袞と親しかった。二人とも徐州一帯の命知らずで、罪を犯して居場所を失い、芒碭山へ向かって、妖術を使う混世魔王樊瑞と一党を成した。樊瑞が首領、項充と李袞が副将となり、三人は山を占め、仲間を集め、家々を襲って略奪した。樊瑞には風雨を呼ぶ術があり、二人には盾や槍を舞わせ、飛刀や投槍を放つ絶技があった。合力した威勢は赫々として、ついには梁山泊を併呑する野心を抱き、水滸の基盤を奪うと公言し、梁山との争いを起こした。

三人の大言を聞いた宋江は兵馬を集め、自ら芒碭山を征した。同行した公孫勝は、樊瑞の学んだものは邪道にすぎず、正法で制せると述べた。両軍が対陣すると、項充と李袞が先頭に立ち、団牌を構え、投槍を舞わせ、地を転がるように旋風の勢いで宋江の陣へ入った。左右に突き進む勢いを止める者はなく、宋公明は命を傷つけられかけた。呂方と郭盛が方天画戟をそろえて出し、必死に防いだうえ、公孫勝も密かに術で助け、あらかじめ落とし穴の仕掛けを設けていた。勇み立って戦いに夢中になった二人は足元を警戒せず、盾もろとも穴に落ちた。伏兵が一斉に押し寄せ、鉤と縄で生け捕りにし、陣幕の前へ送った。

二人の英雄ぶりを認めた宋江は、自ら幕を出て兵を退かせ、縄を解き、手を添えて幕内へ招いた。酒を振る舞って優しく慰め、天に代わって道を行い、賢者を集める志を語り、暗きを捨て明に投ずるよう勧めた。率直な二人は、捕虜としてではなく礼を尽くして遇される仁義に感謝し、ひれ伏して帰順した。さらに芒碭山へ帰って樊瑞を説得すると申し出た。山では宋公明の恩徳と義気を詳しく語り、術を競って覇を争うことに執着するなと諭した。その後、樊瑞は公孫勝との術比べに敗れ、正道の強さを知った。項充と李袞の懸命な説得を受け、芒碭山の全軍を率いて梁山へ帰順した。三人は共に水滸へ入り、再び離れることはなかった。

聚義の席次では、項充は地飛星、第六十四位に列し、李袞と肩を並べる歩軍頭領となった。二人は団牌と飛刀を使い慣れ、敵陣へ突入し、先駆けて突破するのに最も適していた。激しい難戦ではたびたび最初に入り、敵の陣をかき乱す、梁山歩軍の鋭く止め難い先鋒の一組だった。その後の遼国、田虎、王慶の征討でも、項充は先頭で戦い、軍功を立てた。

方臘征討の江南の戦いは、最も危険だった。軍が歙州一帯へ進むと、項充と李袞はいつものように兵を率いて先陣を切ったが、思いがけず伏兵にはまった。険悪な地形で不意を突かれ、優れた団牌も十分使えず、乱軍の重囲へ陥った。項充は力戦して退かなかったが、ついに無数の刃の下で殺され、戦場に命を落とした。半生、盾を舞わせ飛刀を放ち、行く手を阻まれなかった「八臂哪吒」も、江南の山々で翼を折られた。親友李袞と同じ日に相次いで命を捧げ、凱旋の日を見ることはなかった。その忠勇と凄惨な結末は、水滸の多くの英雄の悲歌の中でもとりわけ壮烈な一筆であり、後人を無念に嘆かせるのである。

萧让，济州人氏，乃一介读书的秀士。其人饱读诗书，写得一手好字，真草隶篆四般书法无.en:
Xiao Rang, a native of Jizhou, was a learned scholar. Widely read in poetry and the classics, he excelled in all four calligraphic styles: regular, cursive, clerical, and seal script. He was especially skilled at imitating famous hands from past and present, producing copies almost indistinguishable from the originals. This earned him the elegant nickname “Sacred-Handed Scholar.” A physically frail man of letters, he originally earned his living in Jizhou teaching pupils and writing for others. He was a close friend of Jin Dajian, the Jade-Armed Craftsman, who excelled at engraving inscriptions and seals. One wrote and the other carved, making them a perfect pair. Among Liangshan Marsh's 108 heroes, Xiao Rang answered to the Earthly Literary Star and held the forty-sixth seat. As a civil officer, he handled official correspondence, proclamations, and written troop assignments.

His recruitment arose from Song Jiang's rebellious poem at Xunyang Tower and Wu Yong's ensuing scheme. After Song Jiang drunkenly wrote the poem on the tower wall, the assistant prefect Huang Wenbing denounced him. Prefect Cai Jiu placed him on death row and sent a letter to the Eastern Capital, seeking to have him transferred there for judgment. Eager to rescue him, Wu Yong planned to forge a reply from Cai Jing, induce the authorities to escort Song Jiang to the capital, and free him on the road. But forging the grand preceptor's letter required someone who could imitate his handwriting and someone who could carve his seal. Wu Yong recommended two outstanding men of Jizhou to Chao Gai: Xiao Rang, who could reproduce many calligraphic hands, and Jin Dajian, who could carve every kind of seal.

Liangshan sent men to lure them out of the city. Claiming that the Sacred Peak Temple in Tai'anzhou needed a stele inscription and written petitions, the messengers offered generous payment. Xiao Rang and Jin Dajian unsuspectingly agreed to go. Halfway there, Lin Chong, Dai Zong, and other heroes appeared and openly invited them to the mountain. Seeing no escape and hearing of Liangshan's loyalty, the two went up and joined. Under Wu Yong's direction, Xiao Rang imitated Cai Jing's handwriting to produce the reply, and Jin Dajian carved and stamped his seal. But they overlooked a crucial detail: a letter between Cai Jing and his son Cai Jiu should not bear a seal reading “Hanlin Cai Jing.” Huang Wenbing saw the mistake immediately and exposed the forgery. Song Jiang and Dai Zong nearly died as a result; only Liangshan's raid on the execution ground and upheaval in Jiangzhou saved them. Though this scheme briefly backfired, the two men's writing and engraving skills became valued assets at Liangshan.

Xiao Rang then took charge of literary work. Most of Liangshan's letters, public announcements, and deployment orders came from his hand, and his fine calligraphy lent distinction to the stronghold. At the great ranking he joined the Earthly Stars as the Literary Star, handling records with Jin Dajian and the other civil officers. Though he did not fight at the front, he was indispensable to the stronghold's planning and written administration.

After the amnesty, he accompanied Song Jiang's army against Great Liao, Tian Hu, Wang Qing, and Fang La in Jiangnan. Throughout these campaigns he managed documents rather than exposing himself directly to arrows and stones. The bloody Jiangnan fighting left the Liangshan heroes dead and wounded in great numbers, but his civil duties spared his life, and he was among those who returned from the southern expedition. When rewards were assigned, his unrivaled calligraphy had made his name in the capital. Grand Preceptor Cai Jing admired him and kept him in the Eastern Capital as a resident tutor in his household, chiefly writing for him. Xiao Rang thus lived comfortably in the capital for the rest of his life and met a peaceful end. From writing for hire to outlawry at Liangshan, then back into lawful imperial service, the scholar preserved his life through his fine brushwork, a rare fortunate outcome among so many heroes killed in battle. His calligraphy and literary ability are still praised by later generations.
萧让，济州人氏，乃一介读书的秀士。其人饱读诗书，写得一手好字，真草隶篆四般书法无.ja:
蕭譲は済州の出身で、学問を修めた秀士だった。詩書をよく読み、真・草・隷・篆の四体すべてに精通する能筆で、とりわけ古今の名家の筆跡をまねることに優れた。臨書は真作とほとんど見分けがつかず、江湖では「聖手書生」という雅号を贈られた。もとは文弱の書生で、済州城内で生徒を教え、人の代筆をして暮らしていた。金石の文字や印を彫る名手、玉臂匠金大堅と親しく、一人が書き、一人が彫る、絶好の組み合わせだった。梁山泊百八人では地文星に応じ、第四十六位に座した。行文や檄文、兵の配置命令を専門に掌る文職頭領である。

梁山入りは、宋江が潯陽楼に反詩を書いた事件と、呉用の計略に由来する。酔った宋江が楼の壁に反詩を書くと、通判黄文炳に告発され、蔡九知府は死囚牢へ入れた。さらに東京へ書状を送り、都へ護送して罪を問おうとした。救出を急ぐ梁山で呉用は蔡京の返信を偽造し、宋江を上京の護送へ出させ、途中で奪還する策を考えた。しかし太師の書状を偽るには、筆跡をまねる者と印を彫る者が必要だった。そこで済州の二人の名手、諸家の字体を書ける聖手書生蕭譲と、さまざまな印を彫れる玉臂匠金大堅を晁蓋に推薦した。

梁山は人を下山させ、計略で二人を城外へ誘い出した。使者は泰安州の岳廟で碑文を彫り、疏文を書く仕事があると偽り、高額の礼を約束した。蕭譲と金大堅は疑わず喜んで同行したが、道半ばで林冲、戴宗らが現れ、山へ招きたいと明かした。逃れられず、また梁山の義気を聞いた二人は入山し、仲間となった。呉用の指図で蕭譲は蔡京の筆跡をまねて返信を作り、金大堅が彫った蔡京の印を押した。ところが見落としがあった。蔡京から息子の蔡九への手紙に「翰林蔡京」の四字の印を使うべきではなかったのである。黄文炳は一目で偽書と見破り、宋江と戴宗はそろって殺されかけた。幸い梁山の好漢が刑場を襲い、江州を騒がせて救出した。二人の技巧は一時裏目に出たものの、書と彫刻の才は以後梁山で重んじられた。

入山後の蕭譲は文墨を専ら担当した。梁山が交わす書簡、布告、調遣の命令の多くは彼の手になり、美しい書は山寨の面目を高めた。大聚義では地煞の文星に列し、金大堅ら文職頭領とともに文書を扱った。陣前で戦うことはなくても、山寨の運営や行文に欠かせない人物だった。

招安後は宋江の大軍に従い、大遼を破り、田虎、王慶を平定し、江南の方臘征討に至るまで各地を転戦した。常に軍中の文書を掌り、自ら矢石を冒すことはなかった。江南の血戦では梁山の好漢の死傷が重なったが、文職であったため幸い命を保ち、南征から生還した者に名を連ねた。戦功への褒賞が行われる頃、その当代随一の書は都にも名高く、蔡京太師に認められた。東京に留められて屋敷の門館先生となり、専ら蔡太師のために字を書き、以後都で安らかに余年を楽しみ、よい最期を得た。人の代筆をする書生から梁山の山賊となり、再び帰順して朝廷へ戻り、一本の優れた筆で身命を全うしたのである。多くの好漢が戦場に死んだ梁山にあって、まれな幸運な結末であり、その書法と文墨の才は今も後人に称えられている。

解宝，登州人氏，与兄解珍同为登州城外猎户出身，乃解珍之亲弟。解氏兄弟世居登州山乡.en:
Xie Bao was a native of Dengzhou and the younger brother of Xie Zhen. Both came from a hunting family outside the city. Their people had lived in Dengzhou's mountain country for generations, and the brothers had followed their elders into the forests from childhood, learning to take tigers and other beasts. They used all-iron, steel-pointed hunting forks and were skilled at setting spring bows and poisoned arrows; many local tigers and leopards fell to them. Strongly built and fiercely courageous, Xie Bao was as resolute as his brother. He was called the “Twin-Tailed Scorpion,” while Xie Zhen was the Two-Headed Snake. Both nicknames came from venomous creatures, suggesting men who were dangerous to provoke and would wound at a touch, while reflecting their hunters' boldness.

His everyday dress matched his brother's: an animal hide over his shoulders, a sharp blade at his waist, and a steel fork in his hand as he moved through Dengzhou's deep mountains and dense forests. Two flying yakshas tattooed on his legs added to his fierce appearance. Throughout the region, everyone knew the Xie brothers as formidable hunters.

Their arrival at Liangshan began with a grave injustice over a tiger hunt. A white-browed tiger with slanting eyes was killing people in Dengzhou's mountains, and the prefect ordered the local hunters to destroy it within a fixed time. Taking the official order, Xie Zhen and Xie Bao went into the hills and set spring bows with poisoned arrows. They hit the tiger, but it rolled down the slope and fell into the rear garden of Old Master Mao's estate. When the brothers demanded its body, Mao coveted the official credit and reward. He denied their claim and instead accused them of committing robbery and violence at his home in broad daylight. His son Mao Zhongyi colluded with Dengzhou's military commandant and bribed the authorities. The brothers were arrested, tortured into false confessions, and placed on death row, with their enemies determined to kill them.

Wrongly imprisoned, they were near death. Fortunately, their cousin Gu Dasao, the Tigress, kept a tavern in Dengzhou. Fierce and chivalrous, she valued family ties above all. Hearing of their plight, she planned a prison rescue with her husband Sun Xin, the Little Yuchi. They also enlisted his elder brother Sun Li, the Sick Yuchi and Dengzhou's military commander, the uncle and nephew Zou Yuan the Forest-Emerging Dragon and Zou Run the Single-Horned Dragon, Yue He the Iron Whistle, and other heroes. Acting together, they broke into Dengzhou's prison, rescued the Xie brothers, and killed the entire Mao household to avenge the injustice.

With nowhere to stay after the prison raid, the heroes agreed to join Liangshan. Its forces were then stalled in their three attacks on Zhu Family Village. Sun Li had studied under the same master as the village's martial instructor Luan Tingyu, so he devised a false-surrender plan. He led the group into the village to act as insiders. Xie Bao entered with Xie Zhen, Sun Li, Gu Dasao, and the others. When Liangshan attacked, they turned on the defenders and coordinated with the army outside, crushing Zhu Family Village. Xie Bao fought bravely and earned merit, then went up to Liangshan with the rest and became a commander.

At the great assembly he joined the Heavenly Stars, ranking thirty-fifth as the Heavenly Weeping Star. He and Xie Zhen both served as infantry commanders. Their hunting background made them experts at climbing mountains, laying ambushes, and shooting game. Whenever a campaign brought forests, dangerous passes, or steep ground that had to be climbed, the brothers were commonly sent first. They both served in the attacks on Zengtou Town, Dongping, and Dongchang.

After the amnesty, Xie Bao fought against Liao, Tian Hu, and Wang Qing, never shrinking from campaigns north and south. In the Fang La expedition, the army reached Black Dragon Ridge, whose pass stood atop a sheer and treacherous cliff. Confident in their hunters' climbing skills, the brothers volunteered to scale the ridge at night and raid the stronghold. They climbed vines and creepers up the rock face, but Fang La's guards discovered them. Logs and stones were rolled down from above, and hooks were used against the climbers. Exhausted, Xie Zhen lost his grip and fell with his fork into a deep ravine, dying in the fall. Xie Bao was attacked below the ridge by a mass of arrows, spears, and halberds and died amid the enemy troops. Both gave their lives at Black Dragon Ridge on the same day. From the wrongful tiger case in Dengzhou's forests to their deaths for the country on a Jiangnan cliff, the Twin-Tailed Scorpion and his brother shared hardship, life, and death without abandoning each other. True to the name Heavenly Weeping Star, the brothers' joint fall moved all who heard it to tears, one of the most poignant endings of loyalty and courage among Water Margin's heroes.
解宝，登州人氏，与兄解珍同为登州城外猎户出身，乃解珍之亲弟。解氏兄弟世居登州山乡.ja:
解宝は登州の出身で、兄の解珍と同じく城外の猟師の家に生まれた実弟である。解氏は代々登州の山里に住み、狩りを生業としていた。兄弟は幼い頃から父たちと山林へ入り、虎や獣を捕らえる優れた技を学んだ。総鉄の鋼先の叉を使い、仕掛け弓や毒矢にも巧みで、登州の虎豹の多くがその手に倒れた。解宝は頑健な体に激しい勇気を備え、兄と同じく剛烈で果断だったため、江湖で「双尾蝎」と呼ばれた。兄の解珍は「両頭蛇」で、二人の異名はいずれも毒を持つ生き物に由来する。触れれば傷つけられる凶猛さと、猟師としての勇悍な本性を表していた。

日頃の装束も兄と変わらず、獣皮をまとい、腰に鋭い刃を下げ、鋼叉を手にして、登州の深山密林に出没した。両脚には飛天夜叉を二つ彫っており、いっそう凶悍な姿を見せた。登州一帯で解氏兄弟といえば、山中の手強い名猟師として知らぬ者はなかった。

梁山入りは、虎狩りをめぐる大きな冤罪に始まった。登州の山に、吊り目で白い額の虎が現れて人を傷つけたため、知府は管内の猟師に期限を切って捕殺を命じた。解珍と解宝は公文書を受け、山に仕掛け弓と毒矢を設け、虎を射た。ところが虎は矢を受けて斜面を転がり、麓の毛太公の荘園の裏庭へ落ちた。兄弟が虎の死骸を返すよう求めると、毛太公は役所から手柄と賞金を得ようと欲を出し、知らぬふりをしたうえ、白昼に押し入って強盗と暴行を働いたと逆に訴えた。息子の毛仲義も登州の兵馬都監と結託して役所を買収し、兄弟を捕らえて拷問で虚偽の自白をさせ、死囚牢へ入れ、どうしても殺そうとした。

無実のまま投獄された兄弟の命は危うかった。幸い従姉の顧大嫂は登州城内で居酒屋を開いていた。「母大虫」と呼ばれる激しく侠気ある女で、骨肉の情を何より重んじた。従弟の冤罪を知ると、夫の「小尉遅」孫新と牢破りを相談した。さらに孫新の兄で登州兵馬提轄の「病尉遅」孫立、「出林竜」鄒淵と「独角竜」鄒潤の叔父甥、「鉄叫子」楽和らを招いた。皆が心を合わせて登州の牢を破り、解珍と解宝を救い、毛太公の一家を殺して冤罪の恨みを晴らした。

牢破りの後は居場所がなくなり、好漢たちは共に梁山へ向かうことを約した。当時、梁山は三度の祝家荘攻めで行き詰まっていた。孫立は祝家荘の教師欒廷玉と同門だったため、偽降して一行を荘内に入れ、内応する策を立てた。解宝も兄や孫立、顧大嫂らと入り込み、梁山の大軍が攻めると内外から呼応し、武器を返して祝家荘を大破した。解宝は勇敢に働いて戦功を立て、その後皆と山へ上り、頭領となった。

大聚義で解宝は天罡に列し、天哭星、第三十五位となり、解珍とともに歩軍頭領を務めた。もとが猟師なので、山を登り、伏兵を設け、獲物を射ることを最も得意とした。梁山の征戦で山林の険しい隘路や登攀を要する場所があれば、兄弟を先頭に使うことが多かった。曾頭市、東平、東昌の攻略などでも、二人は力を尽くした。

招安後は遼国、田虎、王慶を征し、南北の戦いで一度も退かなかった。方臘征討で大軍が烏竜嶺へ来ると、関所は絶壁の頂に高く据えられ、地勢は険悪だった。解珍と解宝は猟師として断崖を登り慣れていることを頼みに、夜に嶺を登って寨を奇襲すると進んで願い出た。蔓や葛にすがって崖を上ったが、守備兵に気づかれ、上から丸太や石を落とされ、鉤でも狙われた。解珍は崖で力尽きて手を滑らせ、叉もろとも深い谷へ落ちて死んだ。解宝も嶺の下で矢や槍戟の集中攻撃を受け、乱軍の中で命を落とし、二人は同じ日に烏竜嶺の下で殉じた。「双尾蝎」解宝は兄と生死と苦難を共にし、登州の山林の虎事件で冤罪を受けてから、江南の絶壁で国に殉じるまで、決して離れなかった。「天哭星」の名に応じるように、兄弟そろっての戦死を聞く者は皆悲しみ泣いた。水滸の群雄の中でも涙を誘う、忠勇の結末である。
